1	# Agent-Ops Schema — Boldteq HR & Performance Tracking Database
2	
3	> **Purpose:** System of record for agent lifecycle management, performance scoring, HR decisions, training, and incident tracking in the Boldteq multi-agent software factory.
4	> **Stack:** Supabase Postgres (local + production), full RLS, audit logging, real-time events.
5	> **Source of truth:** This file. All migrations derive from here.
6	> **Last updated:** 2026-04-14
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Table of Contents
11	1. [Architecture Overview](#architecture-overview)
12	2. [Core Concepts](#core-concepts)
13	3. [Table Reference](#table-reference)
14	4. [Complete Migration SQL](#complete-migration-sql)
15	5. [RLS Policies](#rls-policies)
16	6. [Functions, Triggers, Views](#functions-triggers-views)
17	7. [Usage Patterns by Agent](#usage-patterns-by-agent)
18	8. [Initialization & Seeding](#initialization--seeding)
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Architecture Overview
23	
24	### System Design
25	
26	The agent-ops database replaces the current `registry.json` and introduces structured observability for the 22-agent workforce:
27	
28	```
29	┌─ AGENTS (core identity + status)
30	│  └─ AGENT_RUNS (every execution: task, classification, cost, gates, score)
31	│  └─ AGENT_REVIEWS (periodic HR review: classification, promotion decision)
32	│  └─ PIP_RECORDS (performance improvement plans)
33	│  └─ CAPABILITY_GAPS (skill gaps detected by Roster)
34	│
35	├─ ANALYTICS
36	│  ├─ COST_LOGS (per-run token usage, LLM cost)
37	│  ├─ PATTERN_USAGE (which patterns agents apply)
38	│  └─ DELEGATION_GRAPH (inter-agent task handoff tracking)
39	│
40	├─ TRAINING
41	│  ├─ TRAINING_CYCLES (weekly training runs + rollback safety)
42	│  └─ TRAINING_PATCHES (per-agent patch per cycle + rollback)
43	│
44	├─ AUDIT & COMPLIANCE
45	│  ├─ INCIDENTS (production bugs traced to agent work)
46	│  ├─ MEMORY_UPDATES (every change to ~/.claude/memory/)
47	│  ├─ YASH_OVERRIDES (every time Yash corrects an agent)
48	│  └─ PROPOSED_PATTERNS (Mira's semi-auto detected patterns awaiting approval)
49	│
50	└─ REAL-TIME EVENTS
51	   └─ AGENT_EVENTS (event bus: task_started, task_completed, gate_passed, etc.)
52	```
53	
54	### Key Features
55	
56	- **Composite scoring:** Weighted (gate_pass_rate 40%, first_try_success 30%, rework_cycles 20%, yash_override_rate 10%)
57	- **Adaptive promotion:** Cadence compares agent to peer average (same level, same 14-day window) — promotes if consistently above
58	- **Training patches:** Tutor applies pattern patches per agent after every build, with rollback hash for safety
59	- **Full observability:** Event stream captures every task state change, gate result, cost spike, retry
60	- **Audit trail:** Every memory change, Yash override, and incident is logged with context
61	- **Cost tracking:** Per-run token count, model, and USD cost for ROI analysis
62	- **RLS-enabled:** Service role (internal) can do everything; all tables RLS-protected for Boldteq standards
63	
64	---
65	
66	## Core Concepts
67	
68	### Agent Levels
69	
70	**4-tier system:**
71	1. **Probation** (level=1) — New agents, 10-run observation period (Witness)
72	2. **Active** (level=2) — Promoted by Cadence, can receive delegations
73	3. **Expert** (level=3) — High-performing, mentors juniors, complex tasks
74	4. **Architect** (level=4) — System-level work, strategy, rare
75	
76	### Agent Status
77	
78	- `provisioned` — Agent definition exists, not yet deployed
79	- `deployed` — Actively taking work
80	- `training` — In Training cycle (temp)
81	- `pip` — Performance Improvement Plan active
82	- `retired` — Removed from rotation
83	
84	### Run Classification
85	
86	- `SUCCESS` — Task completed, all gates passed
87	- `FAILURE` — Task failed, critical error
88	- `TIMEOUT` — Execution exceeded time budget
89	- `REGRESSION` — New failure in previously-working code
90	- `ANTIPATTERN` — Agent used pattern from `patterns/avoid/`
91	- `ESCALATED` — Agent escalated to Yash or higher agent
92	
93	### Review Classification
94	
95	- `PROMOTE` — Advance to next level
96	- `SCALE` — Keep at current level, increase task complexity
97	- `STEADY` — Continue current pace
98	- `TRAIN` — Enroll in training cycle with specific patches
99	- `PIP` — Open Performance Improvement Plan
100	- `RETIRE` — Remove from roster
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Table Reference
105	
106	### 1. agents
107	Agent profiles — replaces `registry.json`.
108	
109	```sql
110	CREATE TABLE agents (
111	  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
112	  name text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
113	  title text NOT NULL,
114	  department text NOT NULL,
115	  phase text NOT NULL,
116	  level int NOT NULL DEFAULT 2,
117	  level_title text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (
118	    CASE level
119	      WHEN 1 THEN 'Probation'
120	      WHEN 2 THEN 'Active'
121	      WHEN 3 THEN 'Expert'
122	      WHEN 4 THEN 'Architect'
123	      ELSE 'Unknown'
124	    END
125	  ) STORED,
126	  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'deployed',
127	  reports_to uuid REFERENCES agents(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
128	  skills jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
129	  stats jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{
130	    "run_count": 0,
131	    "success_rate": 0.0,
132	    "avg_composite_score": 0.0,
133	    "total_cost_usd": 0.0,
134	    "last_run_at": null
135	  }'::jsonb,
136	  hired_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
137	  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
138	  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
139	);
140	
141	COMMENT ON TABLE agents IS 'Agent identity, role, level, and running stats. Replaces registry.json.';
142	COMMENT ON COLUMN agents.skills IS 'Array of skill tags: ["DB", "API", "UI", "Testing", "DevOps", "Security"]';
143	COMMENT ON COLUMN agents.stats IS 'Running aggregate: run_count, success_rate, avg_composite_score, total_cost_usd, last_run_at';
144	```
145	
146	### 2. agent_runs
147	Every agent execution — the core event for performance analysis.
148	
149	```sql
150	CREATE TABLE agent_runs (

1	# Polyglot SDK Specification — Agent Dispatch & Observability System
2	
3	> **Status:** Production Design Spec (Ready for Implementation)
4	> **Scope:** Boldteq agents ONLY (internal agent-to-agent calls, not external APIs)
5	> **Component of:** Boldteq Software Factory v2 (2026-04)
6	> **Dashboard Host:** Polyglot Hub (Next.js 16 on Railway)
7	> **Database:** Supabase `agent-ops` (separate from app databases)
8	> **Last Updated:** 2026-04-14
9	
10	---
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	**Polyglot SDK** enables all 22+ Boldteq agents to:
15	1. **Dispatch tasks to each other** — call another agent programmatically
16	2. **Emit observability events** — full audit trail of every action
17	3. **Track execution metrics** — performance, cost, gates, retries
18	4. **Self-manage lifecycle** — promotions, PIPs, training integration
19	5. **Provide dashboards** — leaderboards, run history, pattern reviews, cost tracking
20	
21	The SDK is a **TypeScript module** (`@boldteq/polyglot`) that every agent imports and uses at initialization. It reads/writes to a dedicated Supabase project (`agent-ops`) which is independent from application databases.
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Architecture Overview
26	
27	```
28	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
29	│              Polyglot Hub Dashboard                          │
30	│        (Next.js 16.2.3 on Railway, public UI)               │

32	│  - Run history (timeline, filters, search)                  │

39	└─────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
40	                      │ reads from
41	                      ▼
42	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
43	│             Supabase agent-ops (private)                     │
44	│  Separate from app databases. 15 tables:                    │
45	│  - agents                                                   │
46	│  - agent_runs                                               │
47	│  - agent_events                                             │
48	│  - agent_gates                                              │
49	│  - agent_delegations                                        │

62	│        @boldteq/polyglot SDK (TypeScript 5.x)               │
63	│    Installed at ~/.claude/sdk/polyglot/ (Git submodule)     │
64	│                                                              │
65	│  Modules:                                                    │
66	│  - client.ts      → PolyglotClient class                    │
67	│  - dispatch.ts    → Agent-to-agent RPC                      │

74	└─────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
75	                      │ imported by

77	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
78	│          All 22+ Boldteq Agents                              │
79	│                                                              │
80	│  Required integration per agent:                            │
81	│  1. Import @boldteq/polyglot at start of every run          │
82	│  2. Call initPolyglot(config) with agentId                  │
83	│  3. Create RunTracker for every task                        │
84	│  4. Emit task_started, gate results, file changes           │
85	│  5. Log cost at end (model, tokens, USD)                    │
86	│  6. Call run.end() which inserts agent_run + computes score │
87	│                                                              │
88	│  Agents (22):                                               │
89	│  Scout, Vex, Sage | Atlas, Arya, Riko, Ledger |            │
90	│  Rex, Nova, Koda, Dato, Luna, Quill, Vega, Zeph |          │
91	│  Echo, Mira, Bolt, Hawk | Orbit, Pulse, Verdict |          │
92	│  Cadence, Roster, Witness, Forge, Tutor                    │
93	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
94	```
95	
96	### Data Flow Example: Koda Builds a Feature
97	
98	```
99	Koda starts a feature build task:
100	
101	1. Koda imports @boldteq/polyglot
102	2. Koda calls initPolyglot({ agentId: KODA_UUID, agentName: 'koda' })
103	3. Koda creates RunTracker('feature_build')
104	4. run.start() → emits task_started event
105	5. Koda builds the feature
106	6. Koda needs schema → calls poly.dispatch({ targetAgent: 'dato', taskType: 'create_table', ... })
107	7. Dato returns table name, Koda logs logDelegation('dato', 'create_table', true)
108	8. Koda runs tsc, lint, build → run.addGateResult('tsc_no_emit', true), etc.
109	9. Koda modifies 5 files → run.addFileChange('src/app/dashboard/page.tsx') × 5
110	10. Koda runs tests → run.addGateResult('test', true)
111	11. Koda logs costs → poly.logCost({ model: 'claude-opus-4-6', inputTokens: 45000, ... })
112	12. Koda calls run.end() which:
113	    - Inserts to agent_runs table
114	    - Inserts all collected events
115	    - Computes composite_score (gates, retries, cost)
116	    - Returns AgentRun with metrics
117	13. Polyglot Hub dashboard updates in real-time
118	14. Mira loads the run, extracts lessons, updates memory brain
119	```
120

122

127	├── package.json                    # @boldteq/polyglot v1.0.0
128	├── tsconfig.json
129	├── src/

136	│   ├── patterns.ts                 # Pattern usage tracking
137	│   ├── types.ts                    # All TypeScript interfaces
138	│   ├── schema.ts                   # Zod validation schemas

140	├── dist/

145	
146	### Key Files Explained
147	
148	**`types.ts`** — All TypeScript interfaces (68 exports):
149	- `PolyglotConfig`, `PolyglotClient`
150	- `DispatchOptions`, `DispatchResult`
151	- `RunTracker`, `AgentRun`, `AgentRunInsert`
152	- `EventType`, `EventPayload` (16 types)
153	- `CostEntry`, `PatternUsageEntry`
154	- `Pagination`, `QueryOptions`
155	- Supabase table types (auto-generated)
156	
157	**`client.ts`** — PolyglotClient class (main entry point):
158	- `constructor(config)`
159	- `dispatch(options)`
160	- `emit(eventType, payload)`
161	- `createRunTracker(taskType)`
162	- `logCost(entry)`
163	- `trackPatternUsage(pattern, outcome)`
164	
165	**`dispatch.ts`** — Agent-to-agent RPC:
166	- `dispatch()` sends task to another agent via Supabase queue
167	- Timeout handling (default 25 min for builders, 5 min for scouts)
168	- Error handling & retries (max 3)
169	- Cost tracking per dispatch
170	
171	**`tracking.ts`** — RunTracker class:
172	- `start()` → marks start, emits task_started
173	- `addGateResult(gate, passed)` → tracks validation gates
174	- `addRetry(reason)` → tracks retry attempts
175	- `addFileChange(path)` → file mutation tracking
176	- `markOverride()` → Yash override flag
177	- `end(classification?)` → inserts to DB, computes metrics
178	
179	**`events.ts`** — Event system:
180	- `emit(eventType, payload)` → validates & writes to agent_events
181	- Schema validation (Zod)
182	- Timestamp normalization
183	- Duplicate deduplication (same event within 100ms = skip)
184	
185	**`costs.ts`** — Token accounting:
186	- `logCost({ model, inputTokens, outputTokens, costUsd })`
187	- Validates against token pricing tables
188	- Aggregates cost per run

1	# @boldteq/agents SDK
2	
3	The SDK is a small npm package that lets any Boldteq project call any Claude agent programmatically — from a loader, action, API route, or script. One function. No subprocess management. No SSE parsing.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Architecture
8	
9	```
10	Your app code
11	  → callAgent('quill', 'Write listing for Pinzo')
12	    → POST http://localhost:3847/api/playground/run
13	      → Polyglot reads ~/.claude/agents/quill.md
14	        → Spawns: claude -p "[system prompt]\n\n[user prompt]"
15	          → Streams SSE output back
16	            → SDK parses SSE, returns structured result
17	```
18	
19	- **Zero extra cost** — uses your existing Claude subscription.
20	- **Never throws** — all errors are returned in `result.error`, never thrown.
21	- **Requires Polyglot running** — if `localhost:3847` is unreachable, the call fails immediately with a clear error message.
22	- **Server-side only** — use in loaders, actions, API routes, and scripts only.
23	
24	> **Caution:** Never import `@boldteq/agents` in browser code. It calls `localhost:3847` which is a server-only endpoint and will fail in the browser.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## SDK Files
29	
30	Located at `polyglot/sdk/`:
31	
32	| File | What it contains |
33	|------|-----------------|
34	| `sdk/package.json` | Package name `@boldteq/agents`, entry point, TypeScript types reference |
35	| `sdk/index.js` | Runtime — `callAgent`, `listAgents`, `isOnline` |
36	| `sdk/index.d.ts` | TypeScript declarations — `AgentResult`, `Agent` interfaces |
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Installation
41	
42	### Option A — Via Polyglot UI (recommended)
43	
44	1. Open http://localhost:3847/setup
45	2. Find your project in the table
46	3. Click "Install SDK"
47	4. Polyglot adds the dependency to `package.json` and runs `npm install`
48	
49	### Option B — Manual
50	
51	**Step 1.** Add to `package.json` dependencies:
52	
53	```json
54	{
55	  "dependencies": {
56	    "@boldteq/agents": "file:../polyglot/sdk"
57	  }
58	}
59	```
60	
61	The `file:` path is relative to the project root. All active projects are siblings of `polyglot/`, so the path is always `file:../polyglot/sdk`.
62	
63	> **Caution:** The `file:` path resolves at install time. If the project moves to a different folder depth relative to `polyglot/`, update the path and re-run `npm install`.
64	
65	If your project is nested deeper:
66	```
67	~/Desktop/Boldteq App/MyProject/        → file:../polyglot/sdk
68	~/Desktop/Boldteq App/apps/MyProject/   → file:../../polyglot/sdk
69	```
70	
71	**Step 2.** Install:
72	
73	```bash
74	cd "/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/MyProject"
75	npm install
76	```
77	
78	**Step 3.** Verify:
79	
80	```bash
81	node -e "
82	const { isOnline, listAgents } = require('@boldteq/agents');
83	Promise.all([isOnline(), listAgents()]).then(([online, agents]) => {
84	  console.log('Online:', online);
85	  console.log('Agents:', agents.length);
86	});
87	"
88	```
89	
90	Expected:
91	```
92	Online: true
93	Agents: 12
94	```
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Full API Reference
99	
100	### `callAgent(agentName, prompt, timeoutMs?)`
